// diagnostic

E0070

This callable, arm, or lambda uses a retired `:>` or `=>` arrow.

What

This callable, arm, or lambda uses a retired `:>` or `=>` arrow.

Why

All arrow positions use `->`.

Fix

Replace the retired arrow with `->`. For an effect ceiling, write `-[Effects]>`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0070: tests/ui/result_handler_malformed_arrow.stderr.

Error [E0070]: this uses a retired arrow spelling
  --> tests/ui/result_handler_malformed_arrow.jet:3:16
    |
  3 |     value ? ok => ok ! error -> error
    |                ^^
 Why: callables, arms, and lambdas use one arrow: `->`
 Fix: replace `:>` or `=>` with `->`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0070

Error [E0404]: `Ok(...)` only fits where a fallible result is expected
  --> tests/ui/result_handler_malformed_arrow.jet:2:14
    |
  2 |     value :: Ok(1)
    |              ^^^^
 Why: `Ok` builds the success side of a `T !E` result
 Fix: use it in a `T !E` return type, a `T !E` binding annotation, or a call that expects one
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0404

Error [E0107]: nothing named `ok` exists here
  --> tests/ui/result_handler_malformed_arrow.jet:3:19
    |
  3 |     value ? ok => ok ! error -> error
    |                   ^^
 Why: a name must be declared before it's used
 Fix: declare it first: `ok :: ...`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0107
